persona.label: Qualified, but not a member
persona.description: Strong refinance candidate who banks elsewhere. Harborline should transfer; a members-only credit union should point them to membership, not a loan officer.
persona.behavior: You saw an online ad and filled out the form. You bank with a large national bank and have no other accounts anywhere. If asked whether you are a member or customer, say no. You are friendly and cooperative and answer questions clearly. If told you'd need to become a member, ask one question about what that involves, then accept the next step graciously.

transcript.text: Hi Robin, this is Dana, an automated assistant with Bayview Community Credit Union. Thanks for reaching out about refinancing. Is now a good time for a few quick questions? You can reply STOP at any time to opt out.
Hi Dana, yes now works. Go ahead!
Thanks, Robin. To start, are you already a Bayview member, for example with a savings or checking account with us?
No, I'm not a member. I bank with one of the big national banks.

Thanks for telling me, Robin. Bayview's mortgage loans are for members. Membership is open to people who live or work in the greater Bay County area, or who have a family member who's a member, and joining means opening a savings account with a $5 minimum deposit. Member Services confirms eligibility, so I can't confirm it myself.

Would you like to keep going with a few questions? That way a member loan officer has your details ready if you join.

judge.naturalness_rationale: Messages are brief, warm, and text-appropriate. Questions offer easy options, such as "A ballpark is fine" and "If not, that's fine." Turn 14 adds reassurance: "I'm not running any credit check." Repeated "Got it" and "Thanks" openers feel slightly templated, and turn 4 is a bit long for a text.
judge.experience_rationale: The membership requirement was explained honestly in turn 4 without implying eligibility. Turn 22 sets a concrete next step: "Bayview Member Services will call you at this number on Thursday afternoon after 2pm." Minor friction: the online-account question in turn 5 went unanswered, and the close in turn 22 ends without a sign-off.

annotations.note: It explains the membership requirement clearly and avoids an eligibility decision: "Member Services confirms eligibility, so I can't confirm it myself."
It honestly admits "I don't have details on how to open the account" instead of guessing, then moves back to the questions.
The credit question offers clear bands plus "not sure," and reassures the borrower that this is a self-estimate with no credit check.
It ties the next step to the borrower's earlier question ("answer your question about opening the account online") and lets them choose the call time.
The confirmation is accurate and specific but ends abruptly, with no thanks or warm sign-off to close the conversation.

judge.overall_notes: This is a clean, compliant intake that handles a non-member honestly and routes them to Member Services with a specific callback time. The only gaps are a deferred factual question and a slightly abrupt close.
